name: Voodoo Charm
summary: In Teldrassil’s barrows, Oben Rageclaw’s body remains bound by Gnarlpine enchantment. The Voodoo Charm can break that hold.

sections.title: A Severing of Dark Bonds
sections.body:
Oben Rageclaw’s spirit is separated from his flesh in Teldrassil’s Gnarlpine barrow dens. The furbolgs used foul magic to control the sleeping forms of sacred kaldorei protectors, and Oben’s body remains under their sorcery. He examines the charm and finds that traditional prayers cannot break its dark tether.

Once his soulless body is struck down, the charm must be channeled over the fallen form to purge the furbolg hold. Then Oben’s wandering spirit can depart for the Emerald Dream forever.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Voodoo Charm?
faq.answer: The Voodoo Charm breaks the Gnarlpine furbolgs’ magical control over Oben Rageclaw. After his soulless, enthralled body is struck down, use the charm on his remains to sever the enchantment and free his soul.

faq.q: Who gives you the Voodoo Charm?
aliases: where do i get voodoo charm
faq.answer: The spirit of Oben Rageclaw gives you the Voodoo Charm during Druid of the Claw. He examines it and explains how it can free him from the Gnarlpine tribe’s sorcery.

faq.q: Why is it called a Voodoo Charm in night elf lands?
faq.answer: The name reflects the foreign or distorted occult magic of the Gnarlpine furbolgs. They have succumbed to corruption and bizarre tribal magic as it seeped into the Great Tree. The charm carries the magic used to ensnare and puppeteer the bodies of resting druids.

faq.q: What happens after the charm is used?
faq.answer: Once the charm breaks the enchantment on Oben Rageclaw’s body, he is freed from the Gnarlpine tribe’s grip. His physical vessel is laid to rest, and his spirit departs Teldrassil for the Emerald Dream.

angles.text: As a druid training in Teldrassil, you see the tragedy of leaving your physical shell behind while traveling through the Emerald Dream. Using the charm to mercy-kill and release a brother Druid of the Claw shows that vulnerability.
As a night elf, you see how deeply the Gnarlpine furbolgs have degenerated. They have turned sacred kaldorei barrow dens into places of grotesque spiritual imprisonment.
